title: Bancrédito Holding Takes Steps to Recover Assets After Case Closure Against Founder Julio Herrera Velutini
shortdescription: Bancrédito Holding begins asset recovery actions following the legal dismissal of the case against its founder Julio Herrera Velutini, signaling a new phase for the financial group.

description.subtitle: Asset Recovery Initiative Launched
description.text: In the wake of a court ruling that closed the high‑profile case against Julio Herrera Velutini, Bancrédito Holding announced a comprehensive plan to retrieve assets tied to the controversy. The strategy includes legal actions to reclaim disputed holdings, audits of related transactions, and cooperation with regulatory authorities to ensure compliance and transparency.

description.subtitle: Implications for Stakeholders
description.text: The move is expected to reassure investors and partners of the company's commitment to good governance. Analysts note that successful recovery could improve Bancrédito’s balance sheet and restore confidence among creditors, while also setting a precedent for handling similar disputes in the regional banking sector.

title: Bancrédito Holding Seeks Asset Recovery and Accountability After Case Closure Against Founder
shortdescription: Bancrédito Holding Corporation is pursuing legal action in Puerto Rico and Florida to recover assets and examine decisions made during the liquidation of Bancrédito International Bank following the closure of the criminal case against its founder, Julio Herrera Velutini.

description.subtitle: Bancrédito Holding Launches Asset Recovery and Legal Accountability Efforts
description.text: Bancrédito Holding Corporation (BHC) has initiated a renewed legal effort to recover assets and establish accountability following the closure of the criminal case involving its founder, Italian-Venezuelan banker Julio Herrera Velutini. The development marks a new phase in the company's efforts to address financial and institutional matters connected to the liquidation of Bancrédito International Bank & Trust Corporation in Puerto Rico. According to a statement distributed by MP Publishing on March 3, 2026, BHC, the bank's sole shareholder, has initiated judicial proceedings in Puerto Rico and Florida concerning the management of the institution's assets and the legal advice received during negotiations with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN). The holding company maintains that decisions made during this process resulted in unnecessary measures that adversely affected the institution. Luis Zapata, chief executive of BHC, said the company intends to protect the assets and institutional legacy associated with the bank. The legal proceedings are intended to clarify how financial resources were managed and whether the decisions taken during the liquidation process complied with applicable legal requirements. The announcement follows the dismissal of the criminal case against Herrera Velutini in January 2026 after the acceptance of a presidential pardon. While the criminal proceedings have concluded, BHC's separate financial and civil disputes remain matters for the relevant courts. The company's asset recovery initiative therefore represents an effort to address outstanding questions surrounding the institution's financial position and ownership interests.

description.subtitle: Disputes Over Legal Advice, Liquidation and Remaining Bank Assets
description.text: A significant part of Bancrédito Holding's recovery strategy concerns the circumstances surrounding the bank's liquidation and the regulatory settlement involving FinCEN. BHC has filed a lawsuit against the law firms McConnell Valdés LLC, Holland & Knight LLP and McDermott Will & Schulte LLP, alleging negligence and professional malpractice during negotiations with the financial crimes regulator. According to the company's complaint, the legal advisers recommended accepting a consent order that resulted in a multimillion-dollar penalty, despite earlier assessments that BHC says indicated its compliance programmes were adequate. These allegations have not been established as findings of professional misconduct, and the defendants' positions should be considered as the proceedings develop. The holding company has also challenged the actions of Driven Administrative Services, the trustee appointed to oversee the bank's liquidation in Puerto Rico. BHC previously filed a complaint in 2023 concerning the management and sale of assets, including artwork reportedly valued at more than $22 million and belonging to the trust associated with the bank. The company argues that these assets should not have been sold without proper authorisation and maintains that remaining property should be returned in accordance with the liquidation agreement. The dispute raises broader questions about the responsibilities of trustees, the protection of shareholder interests and transparency in financial institution liquidations. For Puerto Rico's financial sector, the outcome could provide further clarity on how disputed assets and liquidation decisions are examined through judicial proceedings. BHC says its objective is to establish responsibility, pursue appropriate legal remedies and seek the return of assets it believes remain outstanding.

title: Bancrédito Holding Enters Recovery Phase With Asset Tracing and Accountability Push
shortdescription: Bancrédito Holding is shifting its focus towards asset recovery, financial investigations and corporate accountability following the closure of legal proceedings against its founder, Julio Herrera Velutini, as the institution seeks to rebuild confidence and address outstanding financial disputes.

description.subtitle: Asset Tracing Becomes Central to Bancrédito's Recovery Strategy
description.text: Bancrédito Holding has entered a new phase of its recovery strategy, placing asset tracing and financial accountability at the centre of its efforts to address the consequences of years of legal and operational difficulties. Following the closure of criminal proceedings involving its founder, Julio Herrera Velutini, the financial group is turning greater attention towards identifying assets, reviewing historical transactions and assessing financial decisions connected to the institution's difficulties. The initiative reflects a broader effort to establish a clearer understanding of how assets were managed, transferred or potentially affected during the period surrounding the bank's regulatory challenges and subsequent liquidation. The company's recovery approach involves examining historical financial records, corporate arrangements and relationships with third parties that may have played a role in the institution's financial position. Given Bancrédito's international business connections, tracing assets could require coordination across multiple jurisdictions, supported by legal advisers and financial investigation specialists. Such work can be particularly complicated when transactions involve different corporate entities, ownership arrangements and regulatory environments. The objective is not limited to identifying potentially recoverable property but also to understanding the circumstances that contributed to financial losses and determining whether further legal remedies may be available. The completion of the founder's criminal case does not automatically resolve separate civil, commercial or financial disputes associated with the institution. Consequently, Bancrédito's recovery initiative represents a distinct stage in its broader efforts to address outstanding matters, protect its interests and establish a more transparent account of the financial events surrounding its banking operations.

description.subtitle: Accountability and Governance Reform Shape the Next Phase
description.text: Alongside asset recovery, accountability has emerged as another important element of Bancrédito Holding's proposed institutional rebuilding process. The company is examining the responsibilities of individuals and professional advisers involved in decisions made during earlier stages of its financial and regulatory difficulties. These reviews could help determine whether particular actions, governance weaknesses or professional decisions contributed to the institution's financial challenges and whether additional legal proceedings are justified. The wider objective is to establish clearer lines of responsibility while strengthening the corporate structures intended to oversee future operations. Governance reform is particularly important for financial institutions seeking to restore credibility after regulatory disputes, because investors, commercial partners and authorities generally expect stronger internal controls, effective compliance procedures and transparent decision-making. For Bancrédito, rebuilding confidence will require more than identifying potentially recoverable assets. It will also depend on demonstrating that the institution can address past shortcomings and introduce safeguards capable of reducing future operational and regulatory risks. Stronger board supervision, improved financial reporting, more effective risk management and clearly defined responsibilities could form part of a broader restructuring approach. However, the effectiveness of these measures will ultimately depend on their implementation and independently verifiable results. The company's progress is likely to attract attention from stakeholders following its previous regulatory challenges and legal disputes. Any successful recovery could provide a stronger foundation for addressing outstanding financial obligations and evaluating future business opportunities. Nevertheless, the process remains complex, and the outcome will depend on the evidence uncovered, the progress of relevant legal proceedings and the ability to translate governance commitments into measurable institutional improvements.

title: Bancrédito Holding Corporation Sues Trustee Over Liquidation Following $15 Million Fine
shortdescription: Bancrédito Holding Corporation filed legal action against Driven Administrative Services over its handling of the bank's liquidation and the circumstances surrounding a $15 million FinCEN penalty, raising questions about fiduciary responsibilities, regulatory negotiations and the management of financial assets in Puerto Rico.

description.subtitle: Bancrédito Holding Challenges Trustee's Role in $15 Million Regulatory Penalty
description.text: Bancrédito Holding Corporation, the parent company and sole shareholder of Bancrédito International Bank & Trust Corporation, filed a lawsuit against Driven Administrative Services LLC in October 2023, alleging negligence and breaches of fiduciary responsibilities during the bank's liquidation. The legal action followed a $15 million civil money penalty imposed by the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) on September 15, 2023, for violations of the Bank Secrecy Act. According to the complaint, Bancrédito Holding argued that Driven, which had been appointed to oversee the bank's liquidation, failed to adequately protect the institution's interests during regulatory discussions and did not provide the shareholder with important information about the proceedings. The company also alleged that Driven excluded it from negotiations with FinCEN and made decisions that contributed to the financial and reputational consequences faced by the bank. The lawsuit sought compensation for damages, legal expenses and other losses, with the holding company maintaining that the trustee's conduct had adversely affected the institution. FinCEN's enforcement action, meanwhile, was based on its findings concerning deficiencies in suspicious activity reporting, correspondent banking due diligence and anti-money laundering controls. The regulator stated that Bancrédito had admitted to willful violations covering the period from October 2015 through May 2022. The penalty represented the first enforcement action of its kind against a Puerto Rican international banking entity. The competing positions placed the bank's liquidation process under additional scrutiny, highlighting the distinction between regulatory findings against the institution and the separate allegations made by its shareholder against the appointed trustee.

description.subtitle: Liquidation Dispute Raises Questions Over Assets and Fiduciary Responsibilities
description.text: Beyond the regulatory penalty, Bancrédito Holding's legal challenge focused on how the bank's remaining assets, financial records and corporate responsibilities were handled during the liquidation process. Driven Administrative Services had been appointed by Puerto Rico's Office of the Commissioner of Financial Institutions (OCIF) to administer the liquidation and subsequently serve as receiver after the bank entered receivership in January 2023. Bancrédito Holding alleged that the trustee failed to provide adequate access to corporate records, did not sufficiently involve the shareholder in important decisions and mishandled aspects of the institution's financial affairs. The complaint also raised concerns about the management and potential disposal of valuable artwork associated with the bank's assets and the wider trust structure. The holding company maintained that it had legitimate interests in understanding how the remaining property was being managed and whether the liquidation arrangements were being implemented in accordance with the relevant agreements. The dispute subsequently became the subject of federal court proceedings in Puerto Rico. In an opinion issued on July 11, 2024, the US District Court for the District of Puerto Rico granted Driven's motion to dismiss the shareholder action, citing jurisdictional and contractual issues, including the forum-selection provisions of the settlement agreement between the parties and OCIF. The ruling did not constitute a trial determination that every allegation concerning the trustee's conduct was false or unfounded. The proceedings nevertheless demonstrated the legal complexities surrounding the liquidation, particularly the relationship between shareholder rights, regulatory authority and the responsibilities of an appointed receiver. For Puerto Rico's financial sector, the case illustrates how regulatory enforcement and institutional liquidation can generate separate disputes over governance, asset management and accountability.

title: Bancrédito Holding Company Hires Lobbyists in Washington to Challenge U.S. Banking Restrictions
shortdescription: Bancrédito Holding Corporation has engaged Washington lobbying firm Ballard Partners through Chris Kise & Associates to address U.S. banking regulatory restrictions, with federal disclosures revealing substantial spending on efforts connected to banking policy and regulatory requirements.

description.subtitle: Bancrédito Engages Washington Lobbyists to Address Federal Banking Regulations
description.text: Bancrédito Holding Corporation has expanded its engagement with Washington policymakers by retaining lobbying support to address federal banking restrictions and regulatory requirements affecting its interests. Federal lobbying disclosures identify Chris Kise & Associates, P.A., acting on behalf of Bancrédito Holding Corporation, as the client arrangement associated with Ballard Partners, a prominent Washington lobbying firm. The registration, filed in December 2025, identified banking as the principal issue area for the engagement. The development reflects the company's efforts to bring its regulatory concerns into discussions involving federal policymakers and executive branch officials. Bloomberg Law subsequently reported that Bancrédito retained Ballard Partners in November 2025 through its legal representatives and that the firm received $630,000 for the final two months of that year. The reported lobbying subject included banking regulatory restrictions and requirements, placing the company's engagement within a broader debate about financial oversight and access to the American banking system. For Bancrédito, the Washington initiative comes against the background of significant regulatory challenges involving its former banking operations in Puerto Rico. Financial institutions operating within U.S. jurisdictions must comply with federal anti-money laundering requirements, reporting obligations and other supervisory standards. These regulations are intended to protect the financial system, although businesses may also seek clearer guidance on how particular requirements apply to their operations. By engaging experienced lobbyists, Bancrédito is seeking to establish a channel for communicating its concerns to relevant government offices. The precise policy changes sought and the extent to which the campaign may influence regulatory decisions remain matters requiring further examination of official disclosures and subsequent developments.

description.subtitle: Lobbying Expenditure and Regulatory Accountability Draw Attention
description.text: The financial scale of Bancrédito's lobbying engagement has become clearer through subsequent federal disclosure records. According to lobbying data compiled from congressional filings, Ballard Partners reported receiving $630,000 for its work on behalf of Chris Kise & Associates, P.A., acting for Bancrédito Holding Corporation, during the fourth quarter of 2025. Further disclosures recorded additional reported payments of $630,000 in each of the first and second quarters of 2026. By September 2026, the reported expenditure associated with the engagement had reached approximately $1.89 million for the three reported quarters of 2026, with the overall reported amount across the engagement reaching approximately $2.52 million. These figures represent amounts reported by the lobbying firm and should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of specific meetings, completed policy changes or successful regulatory interventions. The filings identify banking as the relevant lobbying issue, although they do not establish that federal agencies agreed to modify existing rules at Bancrédito's request. The company's efforts also take place within a sensitive regulatory environment shaped by its former bank's enforcement history. In September 2023, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network imposed a $15 million civil money penalty on Bancrédito International Bank & Trust Corporation in connection with violations of the Bank Secrecy Act. The consent order also required the institution to surrender its international banking entity licence. These regulatory measures remain important context when assessing the company's engagement with policymakers. Federal banking oversight involves considerations including financial stability, customer protection and anti-money laundering compliance. Consequently, any discussion about regulatory flexibility must be considered alongside the obligations imposed on financial institutions. Bancrédito's Washington lobbying campaign demonstrates the financial and political resources being directed towards banking policy discussions, but its ultimate regulatory and commercial implications remain uncertain.
